newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises 2.447 bln stg in September.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises 2.447 bln stg in September.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups to the private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 2.447 billion stg in September, the British Bankers' Association said.
This was down from the August figure of 3.069 billion and the six monthly average of 3.320 billion stg.
Consumer credit rose by 409 million stg compared with a 442 million rise in August and a six-monthly average of 413 million.
Mortgage lending rose by 417 million stg compared with 607 million in August and a six-monthly average of around 600 million.
BBA director-general Tim Sweeney said bank lending was subdued in September.
"On a seasonally adjusted basis, the overall rise in lending was the smallest since January, reflecting less appetite for bank finance across the economic sectors," he said.
"Persons and the financial sector both borrowed significantly less than of late, whilst industrial and commercial companies made a modest net repayment over the month."

Sweeney said the weakness of mortgage lending had come as a surprise considering the recovery taking place in the housing market. "On the other hand, the growth in consumer credit was close to the recent monthly average."
Lending to the financial sector rose by 481 million stg
